newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SAK SAYS SUPPORTS PAPER UNION ON KEY ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SAK SAYS SUPPORTS PAPER UNION ON KEY ISSUE.

text.p: The Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) said on Monday it will support the paper workers in their key demand to make it harder for the paper industry to employ non-paper workers for maintenance jobs.

Paper Workers' Union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki said earlier that it would be difficult if not impossible for the union to join a centralised pay deal -- seen by many as important for maintained low inflation -- and that his union needs to solve this conflict which is currently set aside.

"SAK is for its part prepared to support your union for a sufficiently long-term solution which fulfills at least the starting point before freezing the issue," SAK chairman Lauri Ihalainen told the Paper Workers' Union congress on Monday.
He said the issue could be solved in many ways if the employers want to and said talks should be started before an incomes settlement is made.
"I believe that this will be significant when your union considers joining a broad incomes settlement," Ihalainen said.

The paper workers union congress which started Monday and will continue until Wednesday is due to outline the union's demands for the next round of incomes settlement talks which is due in the autumn and is to set pay rises for at least 1998.
